This Appeal Having Been Heard And Reserved For
Judgment And Coming On For Pronouncement Of
Judgment This Day Through Video Conferencing At
Kalaburagi, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 12.07.2016 passed in MVC No.780/2015 by the learned V Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Hassan, awarding compensation of Rs.5,94,600/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till payment on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the Insurance company is before this Court in appeal.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 7/3/2015 when he was riding his TVS XL Moped bearing registration NC: 2023:KHC:41305 No.KA-13-EC-6563 near Salagame Road at 5.00 p.m, the Motor Bike bearing registration No.KA-13-E-2511 ridden by the respondent No.1 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result, petitioner sustained injuries to his right leg, right hand and also suffered fractures and his TVS moped was completely damaged in the said accident.
He had taken treatment at Mangala Hospital at Hassan as inpatient for a period of 15 days, undergone surgery with ORIF and he incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, working as a Salesman in a Stationary and Books Center and earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to the said accident, he is not in a position to lift the book bundles and unable to eke out his livelihood.

As the respondent No.1, owner of the Motor Bike had requested the petitioner to get the matter settled amicably, he had not lodged the complaint initially and finally registered the complaint on 12/3/2015.

Therefore,
he sought for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at NC: 2023:KHC:41305 the rate of 12%
P.A. from the date of filing of petition to the date of realization.
3. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, the respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed The Manager vs Jabararama on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155057646/
2 exparte.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contending that the compensation sought by the petitioner is very exorbitant and the same is not justified and that the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he was earning an income of Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Therefore,
prayed to dismiss petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed appropriate issues and petitioner examined himself as PW1, two witnesses were examined as PWs.2 and 3 and Exs.P1 to P14 were marked in evidence.
Respondent has not led any evidence before the Tribunal.

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.5,94,600/-
together with interest at 9% p.a. under following heads:
Loss of income due to disability Rs.4,32,000/- 10000 x12x18 x20/100=4,32,000/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
Medical expenditures Rs. 57,600/-
Attendant charges Rs. 5,000/-
Loss of future prospects Rs. 50,000/-

While coming to such conclusion, the Tribunal held that the income of the petitioner was Rs.10,000/- per month and he had suffered disability of 20% as stated by PW3.
7.
Against the said judgment and award, the Insurance Company has approached this Court in appeal.

8. The appellant- Insurance Company has contended that the delay in filing the complaint was not properly appreciated by the Tribunal and the complainant was an hearsay witness and he was not an eye witness to the accident and that the investigation commenced after five NC: 2023:KHC:41305 days of the accident only to fix the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1.

It is contended that the entire investigation is vitiated by the delay and none of the medical records including the Medico Legal Register did not mention about the involvement of the vehicle owned by respondent No.1.

It is contended that the Tribunal also erred in holding that the income of the deceased was Rs.10,000/- per month and it was not justified in awarding future prospects at Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner.
9. On issuance of notice by this Court, respondents No.1 and 2 did not appear despite service of notice.

3

10. The Tribunal records have been secured and heard the arguments by Sri O.
Mahesh, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company.
11.
The learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company contends reiterated the contentions taken in the appeal memo.
It is contended that the spot mahazar was conducted by the police and the witness, who showed the spot of the accident, was not an eye witness and therefore, NC: 2023:KHC:41305 it is a fake mahazar.
He contends that PW1 in his evidence says that rider of the offending motor cycle was one Raju, but in the chargesheet it is mentioned as 'T.R. Raghu Kumar'.
It is also submitted that PW1 says that the FIR was registered on next day, but there is five days delay which is not explained properly.

It is contended that the investigation by the Investigating Officer has been completed with lightening speed which clearly indicates that the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1 was falsely implicated in order to claim the compensation.
Further, he contends that the Tribunal also erred in holding that the petitioner was earning Rs.10,000/-per month when it had rejected the evidence of PW2-Joraram.
Therefore, it is contended that notional income has to be considered by the Tribunal.

It is also submitted that the functional disability of the petitioner should have been considered at lesser than the disability to the right lower limb and therefore, if the Court comes to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation, there should be re-assessment of the compensation to the petitioner.

A careful perusal of the Tribunal records would indicate that though the accident had occurred on 7-3-2015, at about 5.00 p.m., the complaint was lodged with the police on 12-3-2015 by the brother of PW1.
Evidently, the complainant has not been examined by the petitioner.
A perusal of the FIR produced by the petitioner at Ex.P1 discloses that the brother of the complainant lodged the complaint on 12-3-2015.

It was stated that petitioner, who is his brother was returning on TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA.13.EC.6563 after delivering certain goods to the shop at Salagame road and near Saibaba Temple, the motor cycle bearing KA.13.E.2511 came in high speed and dashed to the TVS moped of the petitioner causing the accident.

He states that one Chandrashekhar who saw the accident informed the complainant Joothram and he immediately went to the spot and found that the petitioner was injured and he was shifted to the hospital.
It was also stated that the rider of the offending motor cycle was present and he also helped the complainant to shift the injured to the hospital.
However, the rider had requested NC: 2023:KHC:41305 not to lodge the complaint as he would meet the expenses of the treatment.
But later, he did not respond to pay the medical expenses.
Therefore, he was constrained to file the complaint and as such there is a delay in filing the complaint.
The said complaint was registered and investigation was done and after completing the investigation the chargesheet was filed on 14-4-2015.

It is worth to note that the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the investigation was done with the 'lightening speed'
cannot be accepted, since the chargesheet is filed on 14-4-2015.

The Manager vs Jabararama on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155057646/
4 13.
The delay in filing the complaint alone cannot be a ground to hold that the accident had never happened.

The Apex Court in the case of Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and Others1 lays down in para 21, as below:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the (2011) 4 SCC 693 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41305 victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.

Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it,
even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
14. When we examine the evidence available on record in the light of the above decision, it is evident that none of the records of the hospital mention about the vehicle number.
However, the records reveal that the petitioner had admitted to the hospital on 12-3-2015 with history of road traffic accident.
No-doubt, hospital authorities had not mentioned the nature of the vehicle involved in the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41305 accident, but nevertheless, they mention that it was a road traffic accident.
15. Moreover, the testimony of PW2 who was the treating Doctor discloses that the petitioner was admitted to the hospital for the accidental injuries and he was treated there.
Therefore, it cannot be said that there is sufficient material to show that the accident is doubtful.
The delayed registration of the case by the police alone cannot be a ground to hold that it is a fake accident.

It is also pertinent to note that the first informant had visited the spot immediately after the accident on a phone call by the said Chandrashekhar and therefore, he had seen the spot of the accident.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the drawing of the spot mahazar by the police is based on hearsay witness.

Under these circumstances, there is no infirmity by the Tribunal in holding that the accident had occurred due to the involvement of the motor cycle owned by respondent No.1 and insured by respondent No.2.
The fact that the vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 is not in dispute.

- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41305 The Manager vs Jabararama on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155057646/
5 16.

Coming to the quantum of the compensation, it is evident that in Ex.P1 it is stated that the petitioner had taken certain goods to a shop on Salagame road and after delivering the goods he was returning on his TVS XL Moped.
The employer of the PW1 is examined as PW2- Joraram.
The FIR states that the petitioner was working in the shop of Jootrama.
It is not known whether both of them are employers of the petitioner.
Therefore, there is insufficient evidence to establish that petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/- per month as stated by PW2 in his evidence.
The Tribunal is justified in rejecting the contention of the petitioner that he was earning Rs.15,000/-per month as per the salary certificate issued by PW3 at Ex.P10.
When the Tribunal has rejected the evidence of PW2-Joraram, the next option available for the Tribunal was to consider the notional income.
The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for the settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalath prescribe a notional income of Rs.9,000/- per month for the year 2015.
In umpteen number of decisions it is held that guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41305 the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the Tribunal should have been considered by the Tribunal at Rs.9,000/- per month.
17. The evidence of PW3 Dr. M.M.Shettar, shows that he is the treated doctor of the petitioner and he has stated that there is 20% disability to the right lower limb of the petitioner.
Evidently, the petitioner had suffered fracture of grater trochantric on the right side and abrasions over right hip and contusion of right hip.
Evidently, the casesheet as well as discharge summary discloses that the fracture was treated with open reduction and internal fixation with the help of the implants.
Therefore, the say of PW3-Dr. Shettar that, there is a disability of 20% to the right lower limb has resulted in functional disability of the petitioner.
It is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has taken the disability stated by PW3-Dr. Shettar as the functional disability.
It has not assigned any reasons to hold that the disability of the petitioner is 20%.

Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court,
the functional disability of the petitioner is taken at - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41305 10%.

Under these circumstances, the compensation is reassessed as: 9000/- x 12 x 18 x 10% =Rs.1,94,400/.
18.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head of 'pain and sufferings', a sum of Rs.57,600/- under the head of 'medical expenses' and a sum of Rs.5,000/- under the head of 'attendant charges' which would not require any reduction.
19. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of future prospects.

Evidently,
there is no reason assigned by the Tribunal as to why the future prospects are considered.

However,
it is relevant to note that the compensation under the head of loss of amenities was not awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, instead of 'loss of future prospects', a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of 'loss of amenities in life'.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.3,57,000/- under the following heads:
